name: S32K144
description: NXP S32K144 Arm Cortex-M4F MCU with on-chip CSEc (Cryptographic Services Engine, SHE-compliant) security module, 64-pin LQFP -- project MCU per README.md. Replaces the MSPM0G3507 (REFERENCES.md [1], superseded); the SLB9672 external TPM (REFERENCES.md [2]) remains dropped -- CSEc provides on-chip per-frame message authentication. As of 2026-08-09 an Infineon OPTIGA(TM) Trust M secure element (REFERENCES.md [45], schematic U2) is attached over LPI2C to add the asymmetric PKI layer CSEc structurally lacks: the SE performs device authentication and ephemeral session-key agreement, CSEc consumes the resulting session key for the hot path. See docs/secure-element-architecture.md, and this file's verification field for what is and is not verified.
verification: MIXED -- feature-level facts VERIFIED, physical pin NUMBERS are an UNVERIFIED PLACEHOLDER PIN MAP, per AGENTS.md SS1.3/SS3. VERIFIED against the local copy of [31] (S32K1xx Data Sheet Rev. 15, 5 March 2026): Arm Cortex-M4F core, 80 MHz (RUN) / 112 MHz (HSRUN) (p.6, Fig.3); on-chip CSEc implementing the SHE (Secure Hardware Extension) Functional Specification's cryptographic function set (p.3 SS1.1); 512 KB flash / 64 KB RAM (p.6, Fig.3); 64-pin LQFP is one of four packages this device ships in (48-LQFP, 64-LQFP, 100-LQFP, 100-MAPBGA -- p.6, Fig.3), document number SOT1699-1 (p.89); real power/analog-reference pin NAMES VDD, VSS, VDDA, VREFH, and a combined VREFL/VSSA/VSS pin (p.13 SS5.4, p.14 short note); real reset pin name RESET_B (p.26); real SWD pin names SWD_CLK/SWD_DIO (p.3, p.77). UNVERIFIED / PLACEHOLDER: the local data sheet explicitly states (p.89 SS10.1) that package pinouts and signal descriptions are in the S32K1xx Series Reference Manual, NOT this document -- that Reference Manual was not obtained this session (nxp.com fetch returned HTTP 403, matching this repo's established pattern for this vendor). Every pin 'num' below is therefore a sequential PLACEHOLDER (1..30 in the order pins are listed here) and does NOT represent a real, datasheet-confirmed physical package pin location -- do not send to fab. This build's own signal-role names (CAN_TX, RS485_TXD, GD_SPI_*, ADC_*, PWM_*, etc., mirroring the naming convention already used in the now-superseded symbols/specs/MSPM0G3507.json) are this build's functional labels, not literal NXP silicon pad names, same convention as before. No TPM_SPI_*/TPM_PIRQ#/TPM_RST# pins are included -- CSEc is an internal peripheral with no dedicated external pins (it is driven by firmware over an internal command interface, not an external bus), so dropping the SLB9672 freed the LPSPI channel that build previously reserved for it, and that channel stays free: the secure element added 2026-08-09 is an I2C device, not SPI. ADDED 2026-08-09 (SE_I2C_SCL, SE_I2C_SDA, SE_RST -- sequential placeholders 28/29/30, same PLACEHOLDER caveat as every other pin here): the LPI2C link and reset line to the Infineon OPTIGA(TM) Trust M secure element (U2, REFERENCES.md [45]). Verification status of that attachment, stated separately from the pin numbers: LPI2C is VERIFIED as an S32K1xx peripheral at family level against the local copy of [31] p.3 Features -- 'Up to two Low Power Inter-Integrated Circuit (LPI2C) modules with DMA support and low power availability' -- and LPI2C appears as an S32K14x peripheral row in the p.6 device-comparison table. The exact per-device LPI2C instance count for the S32K144 column specifically is NOT independently confirmed here: that table's column structure does not survive PDF text extraction, so this build relies on the family-level 'up to two' plus the peripheral row, i.e. on at least one LPI2C instance being present -- the same class of family-wide-peripheral-count claim (rather than a per-pin claim) that builds/6s/50A/CAN_485_faraday/README.md already makes for FlexCAN-FD and LPUART. SE_RST is typed 'output' because the MCU drives the Trust M's active-low RST input ([45] p.17 Table 6, pin 09 'IN'); it is a plain GPIO, not a peripheral function, so it carries no LPI2C-instance dependency. The two I2C lines are open-drain in hardware and are pulled up externally on the schematic (2x 10k to 3V3 per [45] p.12 Figure 2), which is why they are typed bidirectional rather than output. See TODO.md for what would upgrade the pin numbers from PLACEHOLDER to VERIFIED (S32K1xx Reference Manual pinout chapter, or NXP's IO Signal Description / Signal Multiplexing spreadsheet attachment) -- resolving that must also confirm a real LPI2C-capable pin pair and a free GPIO for SE_RST, which this placeholder map does not prove.
